title: MS data for Chp1 is a dedicated chaperone at the ribosome that safeguards eEF1A biogenesis
projectDescription: Cotranslational protein folding depends on general chaperones that engage highly diverse nascent chains at the ribosomes. It is not clear how this promiscuous mechanism ensure efficient production of challenging clients such as highly expressed proteins. Here we find that the biogenesis of the abundantly expressed eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1A (eEF1A) depends on the dedicated ribosome-associated chaperone Chp1.
sampleProcessingProtocol: We used site-specific photo-crosslinking followed by two-step affinity purification and peptide mass fingerprinting identification using LC-MS to identify interactors of the uncharacterised protein Chp1 from yeast (saccharomyces cerevisiae).  An amber mutation (TAG) was introduced in Chp1-HA-Myc-8xHis that leads to the incorporation of photoactivatable amino acid p-benzoyl-L-phenylalanine (pBPa) at position L12. After performing UV-A dependent-crosslinking, the cross-linking products were purified by two step affinity purification: 1) affinity purification of his-tag by Protino Ni-IDA resin (silica matrix) using gravity-flow column 2) immunoprecipitation by myc-trap (magnetic beads) The proteins were in-gel digested by trypsin according to a standard operating procedure. The collected peptides were purified with a ZipTip C18 (Millipore, MA) and then vacuum centrifuged to dryness using a speedvac system. Thereafter the samples were dried and resolved in 30 μL 0.1% FA (formic acid) and further diluted 2 times. The resulting peptides were separated in reversed-phase on a C18-column and electrosprayed on-line to a QEx-Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Finnigan) with 90 min gradient. Tandem mass spectrometry was performed applying HCD.
dataProcessingProtocol: Database search was performed using the Sequest algorithm, embedded in Proteome Discoverer 1.4 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against the database consisted of Saccharomyces cerevisiae proteome extracted from Uniprot, Release June 2018. The search parameters were set to Enzyme: Trypsin (Fixed modification was Carbamidomethyl (C), and variable modifications were Oxidation (M), Deamidated (NQ). The search criteria for protein identification were set to at least two matching peptides of 95% confidence level per protein.
